newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open flat to lower.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open flat to lower.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were called to open flat to weaker Wednesday as gold languished overnight with the focus still on platinum group metals and Russian supply.
COMEX June gold was called unchanged from Tuesday's close of $343.40 an ounce. June traded $344.00 to $343.00 on ACCESS.
Early bullion was quoted at $342.50/$343.00, and London gold fixed at $342.25 this morning, up $0.75.
COMEX July silver was called flat to off 2.00 cents and traded $4.72 to $4.69 on ACCESS.
COMEX gold stocks on Tuesday fell 1,544 ounces to 892,391 ounces, while the exchange's silver stocks rose 1,130,938 ounces to 194,404,430 ounces.
NYMEX July platinum and NYMEX June palladium were called unchanged.

The volume of Russian deliveries of platinum group metals in 1997, due to start soon, will be about the same as in 1996, a source at Almazjuvelirexport, the Russian platinum group metals exporter, said.
